The morning begins at Mistico Park.

Hanging bridges lead through primary rainforest, letting you see birds, flowers and other vegetation at different heights.

The route covers about 2 miles in total.

The walk takes around 2.5 hours and is suitable for a range of fitness levels.

There are 15 bridges along the route, six of them hanging bridges.

Some sections offer views of Arenal Volcano.

Next is the Ecoglide canopy tour near La Fortuna, at the foot of the volcano.

Professional bilingual guides accompany you on a series of steel ziplines above the forest.

The first Ecoglide section has seven platforms and six cables ranging from about 30 to 360 feet long.

The second section has six platforms and five cables, approximately 140 to 520 feet long.

The Tarzan Swing follows the second section.

The third and final section includes five platforms and four cables. The individual lines are approximately 230 to 1,410 feet long.

The tour offers views of the forest, the volcano and the slopes around La Fortuna.

In the afternoon, take a guided walk at Arenal Volcano 1968.

The trails here are relatively easy and suit a leisurely guided walk.

The lava flow from the 1968 eruption heavily affected this side of the volcano, leaving some stretches with little vegetation.

The trail offers views of Arenal Volcano, Lake Arenal and the extinct Cerro Chato volcano.

Your guide chooses the route with an eye to opportunities to spot birds, monkeys and other wildlife.

Breakfast is included.
Visitors on a hanging bridge in the rainforest near La Fortuna, Costa Rica
La Fortuna, Costa Rica: walking across a hanging bridge in the forest

Today you travel from Arenal to Manuel Antonio National Park.

The drive between the two areas takes about five hours, with a stop along the way for an excursion on the Tárcoles River.

The boat trip along the Tárcoles and into the Guacalillo mangrove estuary takes about two hours.

This part of Costa Rica is known for its American crocodiles, some of which grow up to 20 feet long.

You may also see birds, including scarlet macaws from the Carara Biological Reserve area.

Children may be especially interested in the basilisk lizards, which can run across the surface of the water.

A bilingual guide explains the plants and wildlife of the river and mangrove ecosystems.

After the boat trip, continue to the Manuel Antonio area.

Breakfast and lunch are included.
